analysis:
The only change in this PR is documentation in docs/provider/cli-reference.md, lines 1045-1062 on the head side. It rewrites the `darkbloom status` `Traffic:` bullet. It adds that the verdict is judged from current evidence only and that the provider re-registers on the same verdict. It adds a new `eligible` path: a request the coordinator routed after its latest status, recorded in `coordinator_connection.last_request_at`. It also adds the `not yet eligible` grace window (`statusGraceSeconds` = 90 s) and the `refusalMaxAge` = 60 s cutoff. Finally it adds the `untrusted`/`offline` status causes and the 'unconfirmed' older-refusal wording. The rest of the supplied head text, including the logout, stop, restart, autopilot and addon sections, is unchanged context. I found no new attack surface or security regression in the documentation text.

One point for integration to check: the `last_request_at` path, by which a routed request counts as eligibility evidence, is code behavior I cannot see. The relevant files are `provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Diagnostics/ServingReadiness.swift` and `StatusCommand+Traffic.swift`. If the provider re-registers or advertises readiness from that signal, it must not treat it as serving authorization. T-052/T-053 and TB-011 require authorization to come only from the coordinator-granted, connection-bound App Attest lease or legacy verification. The doc frames this as a diagnostic display and as the provider re-registering 'on the same verdict'. That wording is ambiguous and should be checked against the code. No source code is in this batch, so the point stays unverified and is recorded here, not as a finding.
